# fiber

> **v0 alpha, pre-1.0, not recommended for production.** Interfaces are still moving and may change between minor versions. fiber is a library, not a service: nothing listens. Its one command, `cmd/fiber` (`fiber run`), runs an `.agent.md` definition once in process for local test. The in-memory composition is complete and tested; the Redis and Postgres bus backends and the Postgres store backends pass the same conformance suites as Memory when a Redis or Postgres is supplied (CI's integration job).

> Agent library and low-latency pub/sub bus for agents. Store an agent as a saige definition, make it a member of a channel, publish a typed event there (a Slack message, a GitHub comment, a Jira issue, a schedule), and the run's events stream to any subscriber and are delivered to any surface. The design turns on one idea: where an event arrives and where its answer lands are independent, which is what makes it a mesh rather than a set of integrations. Composes three libraries: saige (agent loop, versioned agent definitions, typed deltas, RAG citations), anchor (durable execution, ledger as truth, replay), and playscape (sandboxed execution nodes, NGAC access control). Go module `github.com/urmzd/fiber`; the root package `fiber` is the composition root a program composes in Go (`fiber.New(ctx, ...Option)`; no service, no config files, no env vars), and Humagen is the platform built on it.

## Key Concepts

- Event: every event is one `event.Envelope` (CloudEvents-shaped: `id`, `source`, `type`, `subject`, `channel`, `time`, `hops`; run events also carry `tenant`, `run`, `seq`, `agent`, `version`, `digest`) whose `data` is a typed body. `type` is the ONLY discriminator and carries the version: `message.posted.v1`, `github.pull_request.opened.v1`, `cron.tick.v1`, `run.delta.text.v1`, `run.completed.v1`, `run.usage.v1`. `Body` is a sealed interface with one struct per type, decoded by `type` in `Envelope.UnmarshalJSON`. A type this build does not know decodes to `event.Unknown`, which keeps the raw bytes (never guessed, never an error); a known type whose data does not decode is an error. `data` is inline JSON. `Envelope.Private` is host data that is never serialized.
- Catalog: every type is registered once (`event.Register(event.Entry{Type, New, Render, Sensitive, OptIn})`) with its decoder, a byte-stable renderer that turns the body into model input, and a sensitivity flag. A type without a renderer fails a test. `Sensitive` means the body carries human-authored free text or private host data: rendered to the model, left out by egress adapters and logs unless the subscriber opts in. `OptIn` families (`run.usage`, `run.context`) reach only subscriptions that name them.
- Channel: where an event is published, a URI built from `pkg/address`: `slack://T01/C02?thread=1699.001`, `github://acme/handbook/issues/42`, `jira://acme.atlassian.net/PROJ-7`, `cron://acme/nightly`. A run publishes on the channel of the event that started it. Control requests go on `control://<tenant>/<verb>/<hash>` (`event.ControlChannel`), matched only by a subscription naming it exactly.
- Subscription: `bus.Subscription{Tenant, Channels, Types, Run, From}`. Default deny: an empty tenant, channel list or type list matches nothing. Prefixes are segment aware: `slack://T01/C0` does not cover `slack://T01/C02`, `run.delta` does not cover `run.deltas.v1`. Tenant is an authorization scope taken from the caller's credential, never from a request.
- Global bus: one bus carries every event (`pkg/bus`: Memory, Redis Streams, Postgres). Every event has `hops`; one over the limit (`bus.DefaultMaxHops`, 8) is refused. Run events are ordered by `seq` within a run (banded per attempt) and re-publishing a reached sequence is a no-op; other events dedupe by `(tenant, id)`. Delivery is at-least-once.
- Membership and dispatch: `pkg/membership` records `(tenant, channel prefix, agent, Rule{Types, Addressed})`; default deny, and by default a member wakes only for events that name it (mention, review requested, assignment, direct message). `pkg/dispatch` listens to a tenant's ingress events and calls `Runtime.Accept(event, member)` for each matching member. It never wakes the agent that produced the event and drops events at the hop limit. A run is keyed `runtime.RunKey(tenant, event id, agent)`, so a redelivery joins the existing run. `slack.session.stopped.v1` starts nothing and is mapped to stop requests for the runs dispatch started on that channel.
- Adapters: ingress adapters (Slack, GitHub, Jira, cron) verify a request, publish one typed event on the surface's channel with the agents it mentions, and choose no agent. Egress adapters (Slack, GitHub, Jira, webhook) subscribe by channel plus type prefix (`pkg/egress`). Connector faces are derived by `connector.RolesOf`: `Trigger` (ingress), `Sink` (egress), `Actor` (native verbs as tools, each emitting `run.action.taken.v1`). slack/github/jira do all three; cron ingress only; webhook egress only; author actor only.
- Definitions: agents are saige `.agent.md` files (YAML frontmatter `apiVersion: saige/v1`, `name`, semantic `version`, `model.use: provider/model`, `model.fallback`, `tools.registry`, `tools.mcp`, `subagents`, `approval.ask`; then the system prompt) plus a fiber `definition.Policy` sidecar (`subscriptions`, `workspace_areas`, `mcp_write`, `knowledge`, `fallback_on`, `approvers`, `self_approval`, `answerers`, `tagged_only`; the zero Policy grants nothing). Stored per tenant in an insert-only `definition.Source` (`Memory`, `Postgres`): Put of identical content is a no-op, of other content under a written version is `ErrExists`; `Retire` stops new runs and keeps every version readable. Fields fiber cannot honor are refused, not ignored. Budgets convert to int64 micro-USD.
- Pin: at accept a run resolves the highest version and writes `definition.Pin{Name, Version, Digest (saige resolved digest), Subagents (exact versions), PolicyHash, Hash}` into its durable input. Every attempt verifies it; a moved digest, missing row or empty digest fails the run terminally (`anchor.NonRetryable`). A newer prompt never runs under an old pin.
- Runtime: `turn.Runtime` is the one seam: `Turn(ctx, def turn.Pinned, in turn.Input, emit func(ctx, event.Body) error) (turn.Result, error)`. `Input{Trigger event.Envelope, History, Instructions, Tenant, Accounting, Park, QuestionTTL, Resume}`. The host stamps run identity on each emitted body. `pkg/turn/native` is the default (saige); `pkg/turn/sandbox.Sandboxed(inner, plane)` runs any Runtime inside playscape under the pinned policy; `turn.Func` adapts a function; `runtimetest.Run` is the conformance suite; `fiber.WithTurnRuntime` installs one. Durability stays anchor (activities `fiber.turn.v2`, `fiber.turn.agent.v2`, `fiber.turn.resume.v2`; v1 names fail terminally).
- Dual publish: `anchor.Emit` writes the durable per-run journal (replay, cursor resume); `bus.Publish` writes the live bus (observers, delivery). The journal is truth, the bus is flow.
- Stop: `runtime.Stop` (or `App.Stop`) records the request on the run in the anchor ledger (`runtime.WithStopLedger`), then publishes `control.stop.v1` on the run's stop channel as the fast path. Each attempt reads the ledger before its turn, listens on the bus during it and polls the ledger as a backstop; the run ends with the terminal `run.stopped.v1` (reason, asker, partial answer), `App.Status` reports `stopped`, it is never retried, and its thread gets the partial answer plus the constant `runtime.StopMarker`. Unknown, finished and foreign runs get the same answer and nothing is written for them.
- Compaction: `native.Compaction{MaxInputTokens, KeepTurns, OnRequest}` (`fiber.WithCompaction`). `runtime.Compact` (or `App.Compact`) publishes `control.compact.v1` on the run's compact channel; the attempt running the turn compacts before its next model call. Live only, not recorded. Every compaction is published as opt-in `run.context.compacted.v1`.
- Usage: every model call is `run.usage.v1` (`event.UsageCall`: fiber's attempt-unique AccountingID, agent, depth, model, requests, prompt/cached/cache-write/completion tokens, cost, context window); a child run a host Delegator ran is reported once as `run.usage.child.v1` (`runtime.ReportChildUsage`). The run's total (`event.RunUsage{Own, Children, Total, Context}`) is on `run.completed.v1`/`run.stopped.v1`, `runtime.Output.Usage` and `App.Status`. Each attempt records its calls on the run (`event:fiber.usage.a<N>#0`) before returning; `event.Tally` counts each AccountingID once. Cost comes only from saige's price catalog, as int64 micro-units with currency and `as_of`; an unknown model reports tokens and no cost. Opt-in for subscribers; chat sinks never render it.
- Parking on a person: a tool in a definition's `approval.ask` (or any saige `MarkedTool`, or a tool implementing `native.Approving` per call) and the built-in `ask_person` tool park the run on a typed `event.Question{ID, Kind approval|choice|reply|delegation, Prompt, Options, Tool, AskedOf, ExpiresAt, Default}`, announced once on `run.parked.v1`. The run waits on the write-once record `event:fiber.answer.<id>#0`, holding no worker. `App.Answer` validates the answer, records it first-write-wins and wakes the run; the continuation rebuilds the parked conversation byte for byte. Expiry (`runtime.WithQuestionTTL`, default 24h) records the default; Stop resolves a parked question as stopped. An approval is never by the requester unless the Policy sets `self_approval`; `approvers`/`answerers` restrict who may answer. `runtime.WithChildRuns` makes a delegation a child run the parent parks on.
- MCP tool providers (`pkg/toolprovider`, `pkg/mcptools`): a definition's `tools.mcp: [{server: p}]` grants the provider's accepted tools as read; `Policy.mcp_write` adds its write tools. `Provider.CredentialScope` is `shared` (default) or `person`: the credential of the person the run acts for (`event.ActorFrom` on the turn's context), found by an `mcptools.PersonResolver` (`fiber.WithPersonCredentials`). A shared credential is never a fallback.
- Webhook body v2: the outbound webhook POSTs the envelope itself with `specversion` 1.0, header `Fiber-Event-Version: 2`, delivery id `X-Fiber-Delivery: <run>/<seq>`, signed per endpoint. An endpoint names `Channels` (required) and `Types`; sensitive data is left out (`redacted: true`) unless it sets `Sensitive`.
- Security boundaries: `pkg/signature` (HMAC over the raw body, verified before parsing, `hmac.Equal`, Slack replay window, fail closed) and the NGAC policy path (default deny, workspace areas and spawn allowlist).

## Key Files

- Leaves: pkg/address/address.go, pkg/signature/signature.go, pkg/attachment
- Events: pkg/event/{body,envelope,catalog,type,channel,run,ingress,usage,unknown,actor}.go, golden bodies in pkg/event/testdata, pkg/event/legacy (reads data written before the union)
- Seams: pkg/bus/{bus,memory,redis,postgres}.go and pkg/bus/bustest, pkg/connector/connector.go, pkg/definition/{definition,resolver,policy,memory,postgres}.go and definitiontest, pkg/membership and membershiptest, pkg/turn/turn.go and pkg/turn/runtimetest
- Composition: pkg/turn/native (saige runtime), pkg/turn/sandbox (playscape decorator), pkg/runtime/{runtime,sandbox,seq,stop,compact,usage,park,legacy}.go, pkg/dispatch/dispatch.go, pkg/egress/{egress,lane}.go
- Connectors: pkg/connectors/{slack,github,jira,cron,webhook,author}/, the mention helper pkg/connectors/mention, shared helpers in pkg/connectors/internal/{httpjson,inbound,render,sink}/
- Composition root: {fiber,app,config,extensions,connectors,knowledge,status}.go at the module root, examples/downstream/main.go
- Example: examples/local/main.go (zero infrastructure, no API key, no network)
- Command: cmd/fiber (`fiber run [-offline] [-policy FILE] [-provider P] [-model M] [-tools] [-json] [-timeout D] DEFINITION MESSAGE`: one `.agent.md` stored in memory, one `message.posted.v1` published, its events printed by type; exit 0 completed, 1 not, 2 bad input)

## API Cheatsheet

- Envelope: `event.Envelope{ID, Source, Type, Subject, Channel, Time, Hops, Tenant, Run, Seq, Agent, Version, Digest, Data, Private}`, `e.Validate()`, `event.Render(e)`, `event.Lookup(type)`, `event.Types()`, `event.Selects(prefix, type)`, `event.ChannelHasPrefix(channel, prefix)`, `event.ControlChannel(tenant, verb, run)`
- Ingress bodies: `event.MessagePosted`, `event.SlackCommandInvoked`, `event.SlackSessionStopped`, `event.GitHub*`, `event.Jira*`, `event.CronTick`, each embedding `event.Request{Text, Actor, Mentions, Attachments, Context}`; `event.RequestOf(body)`, `event.Addressees(body)`
- Run bodies: `Accepted`, `Started`, `Parked{Question}`, `Resumed`, `Completed`, `Failed`, `Stopped`, `ChildParked`, `Text`, `Thinking`, `ToolCall`, `ToolDone` (arguments as compact JSON, left out above `event.MaxToolArguments`, 8 KiB), `Citation`, `Action`, `UsageCall`, `UsageChild`, `Compaction`; control `StopRequest`, `CompactRequest`; money `Cost{Micros, Currency, AsOf}`; `Tally` counts each AccountingID once
- Bus: `bus.Bus{Publish(ctx, e), Subscribe(ctx, bus.Subscription) (Stream, error)}`, `Stream.Recv(ctx)`, `bus.NewMemory()`, `bus.NewRedis(client)` (size it with `bus.RedisPoolSize`), `bus.NewPostgres(pool)`; `bustest.Run(t, factory)`
- Definitions: `definition.Record{Tenant, Content, Policy, CreatedBy}`, `Source.Put/Get/Versions/Latest/List/Retire`, `Resolver.Resolve(ctx, tenant, name)` returns a `Pin`, `Resolver.Verify(ctx, tenant, pin)` re-checks it; stored agents from before the union convert as the upgrade section of docs/architecture/events.md says
- Membership: `membership.Store{Join(ctx, tenant, channel, agent, Rule), Leave, Members}`, `membership.Rule{Types, Addressed}`
- Runtime: `turn.Runtime`, `turn.Func`, `turn.Pinned`, `turn.Input`, `turn.Result`, `turn.StopSignal(ctx)`, `turn.CompactSignal(ctx)`; `sandbox.Sandboxed(inner, plane)`; `native.OpenAICompatible`, `native.Compaction`, `native.WithToolArguments`, `native.WithStrictTools`
- Connectors: `connector.Trigger{Ingest(ctx, publish connector.Publish)}`, `connector.Sink{Deliver(ctx, target, e)}`, `connector.Subscriber{Subscriptions() []Subscription{Channels, Types, Target}}`, `connector.Actor{Actions() []Action}`, `connector.RolesOf(c)`; egress `egress.New(bus, registry, opts...)`; sentinels `ErrUnsupported`, `ErrNotFound`, `ErrUndeliverable`
- Signature: `signature.NewSlack(secret)`, `signature.NewGitHub(secret)`, `Verify(header, body)`; sentinels `ErrSignatureMismatch`, `ErrTimestampSkew`, `ErrMalformed`, `ErrNoSecret`; `DefaultWindow` is 5 minutes and the boundary is inclusive
- App: `fiber.New(ctx, fiber.WithTenant(t), fiber.WithPostgres(pool), fiber.WithBus(b), fiber.WithTurnRuntime(rt), ...)`, `app.Run(ctx)` / `RunDelivery` / `RunExecution`, `app.Close()`, `app.Publish(ctx, e)`, `app.Runtime().Accept(ctx, e, agent) (runtime.Acceptance, error)`, `app.Status(ctx, tenant, runID) (fiber.Run, error)`, `app.Stop`, `app.Compact`, `app.Answer`, `app.ToolsFor(ctx, e, agent) (native.Granted, error)`, `app.Index(ctx, tenant, source, paths...)`, `app.Webhooks()`, `app.WebhookHandler()`, accessors `Definitions`, `Memberships`, `Bus`, `Runtime`, `Dispatcher`, `Egress`, `Connectors`, `Knowledge`, `Threads`, `ToolProviders`, `Blobs`
